Section 12.1: Beyond classical Bayesian model comparison

Section 12.1.1: Schwarz criterion and BIC

Example 12.1: Labor market data: Bayesian variable selection using BIC

We return to the probit analysis of Example 11.11 and run variable selection using the Schwarz criterion instead of the marginal likelihood. We first implement this approach.

modsel_probit_BIC <- function(y, X, burnin = 1000L, M = 5000L) {
  N <- length(y)
  p <- ncol(X)

  gamma_post <- matrix(0L, nrow = M, ncol = p,
                       dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(X)))
  acc <- integer(length = M)

  gamma <- rep(1L, length.out = p)
  mod0 <- glm(y ~ X, family = binomial(link = "probit"))
  SC_old <- logLik(mod0) - log(N) * (p + 1) / 2

  for (m in seq_len(burnin + M)) {
    gamma_proposed <- gamma

    j <- sample(1:p, size = 1)
    gamma_proposed[j] <- 1 - gamma[j]

    X_gamma <- X[, gamma_proposed == 1]
    model <- glm(y ~ X_gamma, family = binomial(link = "probit"))
    SC_proposed <- logLik(model) - log(N) * (sum(gamma_proposed) + 1) / 2
    
    # Compute acceptance probability and decide on acceptance
    log_acc <- SC_proposed - SC_old

    if (log(runif(1)) < log_acc) {
      gamma <- gamma_proposed
      SC_old <- SC_proposed
      accept <- 1L
    } else {
      accept <- 0L
    }

    if (m > burnin) {
      gamma_post[m - burnin, ] <- gamma
      acc[m - burnin] <- accept
    }
  }
  return(list(gamma_post = gamma_post, acc = acc))
}

Next we load the data and add 5 irrelevant, standard normal regressors as in Example 11.11. Then we run the algorithm.

library("BayesianLearningCode")
data("labor", package = "BayesianLearningCode")
y <- labor$income_1998 == "zero"
N <- length(y)
X_unemp <- with(labor, cbind(female = female,
                             age18 = 1998 - birthyear - 18,
                             wcollar = wcollar_1997,
                             unemp97 = income_1997 == "zero")) # regressor matrix
p_irrel <- 5
set.seed(seed)
X <- cbind(X_unemp, matrix(rnorm(p_irrel * N), ncol = p_irrel))
p <- ncol(X)
colnames(X)[ncol(X_unemp) + (1:p_irrel)] <-
  paste0("irrel", seq_len(p_irrel))

M <- 20000 / mcmcspeedup
res <- modsel_probit_BIC(y, X, M = M)

We determine the number of models visited during MCMC, the average model complexity, i.e., the average number of covariates included in the model, and show the posterior inclusion probabilities.

if (pdfplots) {
  pdf("12-1_1.pdf", width = 5, height = 6)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(2.5, 2.5, 1.5, .5), mgp = c(1.5, .5, 0))

gammas <- unique(res$gamma_post)
nrow(gammas)
#> [1] 21

k_gamma <- rowSums(res$gamma_post)
mean(k_gamma)
#> [1] 3.7335

# PIPs
colMeans(res$gamma_post)
#>  female   age18 wcollar unemp97  irrel1  irrel2  irrel3  irrel4  irrel5 
#>  0.8995  1.0000  0.7020  1.0000  0.0320  0.0085  0.0065  0.0710  0.0140
barplot(colMeans(res$gamma_post), col = "blue", names.arg = 1:p,
        xlab = "Covariate", ylab = "PIP")

To determine the models visited most often we re-use a function which we defined in Chapter 11.

number_draws <- function(gamma_post, models) {
  sapply(1:nrow(models), function(j)
    sum(apply(gamma_post, 1, function(x) identical(x, models[j,]))))
}
n_gamma <- number_draws(res$gamma_post, gammas)
io <- order(n_gamma, decreasing = TRUE)
knitr::kable(cbind(gammas, phat_gamma = n_gamma / M)[io[1:5], ],
             digits = c(rep(0, p), 4))

Section 12.2.2: Akaike information criterion (AIC)

Example 12.2: U.S. GDP data: Choosing the model order via AIC and BIC

We need to re-load the function which creates the design matrix.

ARdesignmatrix <- function(dat, p = 1, conditioninglength = p) {
  d <- p + 1
  N <- length(dat) - p

  Xy <- matrix(NA_real_, N, d)
  Xy[, 1] <- 1
  for (i in seq_len(p)) {
    Xy[, i + 1] <- dat[(p + 1 - i) : (length(dat) - i)]
  }
  Xy[(1 + conditioninglength - p):N, , drop = FALSE]
}

Let’s load the data and compute log returns.

data("gdp", package = "BayesianLearningCode")
logret <- diff(log(gdp))

Now we compute five OLS estimates and the corresponding AICs and BICs.

AIC <- BIC <- rep(NA_real_, 5)
names(AIC) <- 0:4
for (i in seq_along(AIC)) {
  y <- tail(logret, -4)
  p <- i - 1     # lag length
  d <- i + 1     # total number of parameters
  N <- length(y) # number of data points used for estimation
  Xy <- ARdesignmatrix(logret, p, conditioninglength = 4)
  fit <- lm(y ~ Xy - 1)
  betahat <- coef(fit)
  sigma2hat <- sum(resid(fit)^2) / length(y)
  minus2timesloglikmax <- N * (1 + log(2 * pi)) + N * log(sigma2hat)
  AIC[i] <- minus2timesloglikmax + 2 * d      # equals built-in AIC(fit)
  BIC[i] <- minus2timesloglikmax + log(N) * d # equals built-in BIC(fit)
}
knitr::kable(rbind(AIC, BIC), digits = 2)
0 1 2 3 4
AIC -1808.61 -1828.87 -1839.65 -1837.66 -1836.24
BIC -1801.15 -1817.68 -1824.72 -1819.01 -1813.86

Example 12.3: CHF exchange rate data: Testing normal vs. t using AIC and BIC

Let’s load the data first and make some space for the draws under the three models.

data("exrates", package = "stochvol")
y <- 100 * diff(log(exrates$USD / exrates$CHF))
X <- 1
N <- length(y)

The maximum likelihood estimator for normal data is known in closed form, while for the tt distribution we have to find it numerically. Thus, we write a function first. To ensure positivity for our parameter(s), we work on the log scale.

mle <- function(y, df = NULL) {
  # We first define the negative log likelihood function. If df is NULL,
  # par is expected to have two elements (logsigma and lognu), otherwise
  # just one (logsigma)
  nll <- function(y, par, df = NULL) {
    sigma <- exp(par[1])
    if (is.null(df)) nu <- exp(par[2]) else nu <- df
    -sum(dstudt(y, 0, sigma, nu, log = TRUE))
  }
  
  s <- sqrt(mean(y^2)) # starting value
  
  if (!is.null(df)) { # Case 1: df known/fixed
    fit <- optim(log(s), nll, y = y, df = df,
                 method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
  } else { # Case 2: df is to be estimated
    d <- 7 # starting value
    fit <- optim(c(log(s), log(d)), nll, y = y,
                 method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
  }

  list(muhat = 0,
       sigma2hat = exp(fit$par[1])^2,
       nuhat = if (is.null(df)) exp(fit$par[2]) else df,
       loglik = -fit$value, convergence = fit$convergence,
       hessian = fit$hessian)
}

Now we can compute the MLEs.

mles <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 3, ncol = 2)
colnames(mles) <- c("sigma2", "nu")
mles[1, "sigma2"] <- mean(y^2) # same as mle(y, df = Inf)$sigma2hat
mles[1, "nu"] <- Inf
mles[2, "sigma2"] <- mle(y, df = 7)$sigma2hat
mles[2, "nu"] <- 7
mles[3, "sigma2"] <- mle(y)$sigma2hat
mles[3, "nu"] <- mle(y)$nuhat

And finally, we compute AIC and BIC.

res <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(mles), ncol = 2)
colnames(res) <- c("AIC", "BIC")
rownames(res) <- c("Gaussian", "t_7", "t_nu")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(mles))) {
  ll <- sum(dstudt(y, 0, sqrt(mles[i, "sigma2"]), mles[i, "nu"], log = TRUE))
  if (rownames(res)[i] == "t_nu") d <- 2 else d <- 1
  res[i, "AIC"] <- -2 * ll + 2 * d
  res[i, "BIC"] <- -2 * ll + log(N) * d
}

knitr::kable(t(res), digits = 2)
Gaussian t_7 t_nu
AIC 6906.93 6605.54 6605.59
BIC 6912.98 6611.59 6617.70

Section 12.2.3: Deviance information criterion (DIC)

Example 12.6: CHF exchange rate data: Testing normal vs. t using DIC

We will store the MCMC draws of the three models in questions.

draws <- vector("list", 3)

Under the zero-mean Gaussian model, the posterior of σ2\sigma^2 is inverse gamma, and we can easily draw from it.

set.seed(seed)
c0 <- 2.5
C0 <- 1.5

SSR <- sum(y^2)
cN <- c0 + N / 2
CN <- C0 + SSR / 2

# number of draws
M <- 100000 / mcmcspeedup

# thinning to save some computer memory (1 = no thinning)
thin <- 1

draws[[1]]$sigma2s <- rinvgamma(M / thin, cN , CN)
draws[[1]]$nus <- Inf

Under the t distribution with 7 degrees of freedom, the posterior of σ2\sigma^2 is not available in closed form, but we can draw from it using data augmentation.

sampler <- function(y, M, burnin, c0, C0, nu, thin = 1L) {
  N <- length(y)
  
  # starting value for w
  w <- rep(1, N)

  # pre-compute cN
  cN <- c0 + N / 2

  # allocate space for storing the draws
  draws <- list()
  draws$sigma2s <- rep(NA_real_, M)
  draws$nus <- rep(nu, M)
  draws$ws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = M, ncol = N)
 
  for (m in 1:(burnin + M)) {
    # sample sigma^2 from its full conditional (S-DA)
    eps <- sqrt(w) * y
    CN <- C0 + crossprod(eps) / 2
    sigma2 <- rinvgamma(1, cN, CN)

    # sample w (W-DA)
    r <- eps^2 / (w * sigma2)
    w <- rgamma(length(eps), (nu + 1) /2, (nu + r) / 2)

    # store the results
    if (m > burnin && (m - burnin) %% thin == 0L) {
      draws$sigma2s[m - burnin] <- sigma2
      draws$ws[m - burnin, ] <- w
    }
  }
  draws
}

Now we can run the sampler.

burnin <- 100
nu <- 7
draws[[2]] <- sampler(y, M, burnin, c0, C0, nu)

For sampling also the degrees of freedom under an exponential prior, we re-run the sampler from Example 8.16, but this time without an intercept.

# fix tuning parameter for MH
cnu <- 0.3

# fix prior hyperparameters
lambda <- 1 / 7

# log likelihood
loglik <- function(y, sigma2, nu) {
  sum(dstudt(y, 0, sqrt(sigma2), df = nu, log = TRUE))
}

# allocate space for storing the draws
draws[[3]]$nus <- draws[[3]]$sigma2s <- rep(NA_real_, M / thin)
draws[[3]]$ws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = M / thin, ncol = N)

# starting value for log(nu) and w
w <- rep(1, N)
nu <- 7

accepts <- 0L
for (m in 1:(burnin + M)) {
  # sample sigma^2 from its full conditional (S-DA)
  eps <- sqrt(w) * y
  CN <- C0 + crossprod(eps) / 2
  sigma2 <- rinvgamma(1, cN, CN)

  # sample nu (N-MH)
  nuprop <- exp(rnorm(1, log(nu), cnu))
  logR <- loglik(y, sigma2, nuprop) -
          loglik(y, sigma2, nu) +
          dexp(nuprop, lambda, log = TRUE) -
          dexp(nu, lambda, log = TRUE) +
          log(nuprop) -
          log(nu)
  
  if (log(runif(1)) < logR) {
    nu <- nuprop
    if (m > burnin) accepts <- accepts + 1L
  }
  
  # sample w (W-DA)
  r <- eps^2 / (w * sigma2)
  w <- rgamma(length(eps), (nu + 1) /2, (nu + r) / 2)

  # store the results
  if (m > burnin && (m - burnin) %% thin == 0L) {
    draws[[3]]$sigma2s[(m - burnin) / thin] <- sigma2
    draws[[3]]$nus[(m - burnin) / thin] <- nu
    draws[[3]]$ws[(m - burnin) / thin, ] <- w
  }
}
print(accepts / M)
#> [1] 0.2928

We can now estimate the DIC from the draws. First, we define the deviance function DD.

D_nonvec <- function(y, sigma2, nu) -2 * loglik(y, sigma2, nu)
D <- Vectorize(D_nonvec, c("sigma2", "nu"))

Before we move on, let us define a function that sorts a vector into batches, and another one which computes the batch-wise means. That way, we can numerically gauge the precision of our estimates.

batches <- function(x, amount = 10) {
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1L || length(x) %% amount == 0L)
  matrix(x, ncol = amount)
}

batchMeans <- function(x, amount = 10) {
  colMeans(batches(x, amount = amount))
}

batchMedians <- function(x, amount = 10) {
  apply(batches(x, amount = amount), 2, median)
}

Now, we estimate the average deviance, the deviance of the posterior averages, the effective number of parameters, and, finally, DIC.

res <- array(NA_real_, c(3, 4, 10))
colnames(res) <- c("DIC", "avgD", "Davg", "pd")
for (i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  d <- draws[[i]]
  res[i, "avgD", ] <- batchMeans(D(y, d$sigma2s, d$nus))
  res[i, "Davg", ] <- D(y, batchMeans(d$sigma2s), batchMeans(d$nus))
  res[i, "pd", ] <-  res[i, "avgD", ] - res[i, "Davg", ]
  res[i, "DIC", ] <- res[i, "avgD", ] + res[i, "pd", ]
}
mins <- apply(res, 1:2, min)
maxs <- apply(res, 1:2, max)
out <- matrix(paste0("[", roun(mins, 2), ", ", roun(maxs, 2), "]"),
              nrow = dim(res)[1])
colnames(out) <- colnames(res)
rownames(out) <- c("Gaussian", "t_7", "t_nu")
knitr::kable(out)
DIC avgD Davg pd
Gaussian [6906.83, 6907.09] [6905.88, 6906.01] [6904.93, 6904.94] [0.95, 1.08]
t_7 [6605.35, 6605.68] [6604.45, 6604.62] [6603.54, 6603.56] [0.90, 1.06]
t_nu [6605.29, 6606.21] [6603.45, 6603.91] [6601.61, 6601.76] [1.79, 2.30]

For the Gaussian model (only), we can compute the DIC in closed form.

cN <- c0 + N / 2
CN <- C0 + SSR / 2
Davg <- N * log(2 * pi * CN / (cN - 1)) + (cN - 1) * SSR / CN
avgD <- N * (log(2 * pi * CN) - digamma(cN)) + SSR * cN / CN
pd <- avgD - Davg
# Explicitly: N * (log(cN - 1) - digamma(cN)) + SSR / CN
DIC <- avgD + pd
# N * log(2 * pi * CN * (cN - 1)) - 2 * N * digamma(cN) + (cN + 1) * SSR / CN
knitr::kable(cbind(DIC, avgD, Davg, pd))
DIC avgD Davg pd
6906.922 6905.925 6904.927 0.997449

Example 12.7: CHF exchange rate data: Testing normal vs. Student t using hierarchical DIC

Because we also stored the weights, we can use the samples from above to compute conditional and augmented DICs. To do so, we first define the log conditional likelihood and the log augmented (“complete-data”) likelihood.

logcondlik <- function(y, sigma2, nu, w) {
  sum(dnorm(y, 0, sqrt(sigma2 / w), log = TRUE))
}

logauglik <- function(y, sigma2, nu, w) {
  logcondlik(y, sigma2, nu, w) + sum(dgamma(w, nu / 2, nu / 2, log = TRUE))
}

Now we can compute the conditional and the augmented DIC.

res <- array(NA_real_, c(2, 4, 10))
colnames(res) <- c("DIC_C", "pd_C", "DIC_A", "pd_A")
for (i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  d <- draws[[i + 1]]
  
  # Evaluate the log conditional likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogcondlik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logcondlik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Compute the average conditional deviance
  avgcondD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogcondlik)
  
  # Evaluate the log augmented likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogauglik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logauglik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Evaluate the unnormalized log posterior
  alllogpost_unnormalized <- alllogauglik +
    dinvgamma(d$sigma2s, c0, C0, log = TRUE) + dexp(d$nus, lambda, log = TRUE)
  
  # Find the index of the posterior draw with highest joint posterior density
  MAPind <- apply(batches(alllogpost_unnormalized), 2, which.max)
  
  # Evaluate the conditional deviance at the MAP
  estcondD <- -2 * batches(alllogcondlik)[cbind(MAPind, seq_len(dim(res)[3]))]
  
  # Compute conditional pd and conditional DIC
  res[i, "pd_C", ] <- avgcondD - estcondD
  res[i, "DIC_C", ] <- 2 * avgcondD - estcondD
  
  # Compute the average augmented deviance
  avgaugD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogauglik)
  
  # Evaluate the augmented deviance at the MAP
  estaugD <- -2 * batches(alllogauglik)[cbind(MAPind, seq_len(dim(res)[3]))]
  
  # Compute augmented pd and augmented DIC
  res[i, "pd_A", ] <- avgaugD - estaugD
  res[i, "DIC_A", ] <- 2 * avgaugD - estaugD
}
mins <- apply(res, 1:2, min)
maxs <- apply(res, 1:2, max)
out <- matrix(paste0("[", roun(mins, 2), ", ", roun(maxs, 2), "]"),
              nrow = dim(res)[1])
colnames(out) <- colnames(res)
rownames(out) <- c("t_7", "t_nu")
knitr::kable(out)
DIC_C pd_C DIC_A pd_A
t_7 [6125.46, 6231.83] [3.55, 108.02] [10705.80, 10784.09] [229.25, 308.95]
t_nu [5901.34, 6091.61] [-179.81, 12.03] [11276.91, 11594.55] [590.60, 861.75]

Our MAP approximation is probably rather bad (remember that we are trying to find the maximum of a high-dimensional function). Let us try to exploit the fact that the conditional maxima of the ws are available in closed form.

# Non-normalized negative joint log-posterior, with w replaced by
# its closed-form conditional mode
objective <- function(par, y, c0, C0, lambda) {
  
  sigma2 <- exp(par[1])     # sigma2 must be positive
  nu     <- 1 + exp(par[2]) # nu must be > 1 for the conditional mode to exist

  # Conditional mode of w_i | y_i, sigma2, nu
#  print(round(c(nu, sigma2), 2))
  w_hat <- (nu - 1) / (nu + y^2 / sigma2)

  # Log likelihood: y | w, sigma2
  loglik <- sum(dnorm(y, 0, sqrt(sigma2 / w_hat), log = TRUE))

  # Log prior: w | nu
  log_w_prior <- sum(dgamma(w_hat, nu / 2, nu / 2, log = TRUE))

  # Inverse-Gamma prior for sigma2 (shape c0, rate C0)
  log_sigma2_prior <- dinvgamma(sigma2, c0, C0, log = TRUE)

  # Exponential prior for nu
  log_nu_prior <- dexp(nu, lambda, log = TRUE)

  logpost <- loglik + log_w_prior + log_sigma2_prior + log_nu_prior

  -logpost
}

fit <- optim(log(c(mean(y^2), 7 - 1)), objective, method = "BFGS", 
             y = y, c0 = c0, C0 = C0, lambda = lambda)

sigma2_hat <- exp(fit$par[1])
nu_hat     <- 1 + exp(fit$par[2])

w_hat <- (nu_hat - 1) / (nu_hat + y^2 / sigma2_hat)

This doesn’t seem to work too well, either. (Thinking a bit about it reveals that the joint mode is degenerate.)

Let’s also try with the posterior mean as point estimate.

res <- array(NA_real_, c(2, 4, 10))
colnames(res) <- c("DIC_C", "pd_C", "DIC_A", "pd_A")
for (i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  d <- draws[[i + 1]]
  
  # Evaluate the log conditional likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogcondlik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logcondlik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Compute the average conditional deviance
  avgcondD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogcondlik)
  
  # Evaluate the log augmented likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogauglik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logauglik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Evaluate the conditional deviance at the posterior mean
  sigma2means <- batchMeans(d$sigma2s)
  numeans <- batchMeans(d$nus)
  wmeans <- apply(d$ws, 2, batchMeans)
  
  estcondD <- rep(NA_real_, dim(res)[3])
  for (j in seq_len(dim(res)[3])) {
    estcondD[j] <- -2 * logcondlik(y, sigma2means[j], numeans[j], wmeans[j, ])
  }
  
  # Compute conditional pd and conditional DIC
  res[i, "pd_C", ] <- avgcondD - estcondD
  res[i, "DIC_C", ] <- 2 * avgcondD - estcondD
  
  # Compute the average augmented deviance
  avgaugD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogauglik)
  
  # Evaluate the augmented deviance at the posterior mean
  estaugD <- rep(NA_real_, dim(res)[3])
  for (j in seq_len(dim(res)[3])) {
    estaugD[j] <- -2 * logauglik(y, sigma2means[j], numeans[j], wmeans[j, ])
  }
  
  # Compute augmented pd and augmented DIC
  res[i, "pd_A", ] <- avgaugD - estaugD
  res[i, "DIC_A", ] <- 2 * avgaugD - estaugD
}
mins <- apply(res, 1:2, min)
maxs <- apply(res, 1:2, max)
out <- matrix(paste0("[", roun(mins, 2), ", ", roun(maxs, 2), "]"),
              nrow = dim(res)[1])
colnames(out) <- colnames(res)
rownames(out) <- c("t_7", "t_nu")

res <- array(NA_real_, c(2, 4, 10))

for (i in 1:nrow(res)) {

  alllogcondlik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logcondlik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Compute the average conditional deviance
  avgcondD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogcondlik)
  
  # Evaluate the log augmented likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogauglik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logauglik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Evaluate the conditional deviance at the posterior median
  sigma2medians <- batchMedians(d$sigma2s)
  numedians <- batchMedians(d$nus)
  wmedians <- apply(d$ws, 2, batchMedians)
  
  estcondD <- rep(NA_real_, dim(res)[3])
  for (j in seq_len(dim(res)[3])) {
    estcondD[j] <- -2 * logcondlik(y, sigma2medians[j], numedians[j],
                                   wmedians[j, ])
  }
  
  # Compute conditional pd and conditional DIC
  res[i, "pd_C", ] <- avgcondD - estcondD
  res[i, "DIC_C", ] <- 2 * avgcondD - estcondD
  
  # Compute the average augmented deviance
  avgaugD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogauglik)
  
  # Evaluate the augmented deviance at the posterior median
  estaugD <- rep(NA_real_, dim(res)[3])
  for (j in seq_len(dim(res)[3])) {
    estaugD[j] <- -2 * logauglik(y, sigma2medians[j], numedians[j],
                                 wmedians[j, ])
  }
  
  # Compute augmented pd and augmented DIC
  res[i, "pd_A", ] <- avgaugD - estaugD
  res[i, "DIC_A", ] <- 2 * avgaugD - estaugD
}

mins <- apply(res, 1:2, min)
maxs <- apply(res, 1:2, max)
out <- matrix(paste0("[", roun(mins, 2), ", ", roun(maxs, 2), "]"),
              nrow = dim(res)[1])
colnames(out) <- colnames(res)
rownames(out) <- c("t_7", "t_nu")
knitr::kable(out)

Finally, we use the actual joint posterior mode of (σ2,ν,w1,…,wN)(\sigma^2, \nu, w_1, \dots, w_N). We find it through simple (block) coordinate ascent: the conditional modes of the wiw_i and of σ2\sigma^2 are available in closed form, and ν\nu is updated through a one-dimensional numerical maximization.

logpost_joint <- function(y, sigma2, nu, w, c0, C0, lambda) {
  logauglik(y, sigma2, nu, w) + dinvgamma(sigma2, c0, C0, log = TRUE) +
    dexp(nu, lambda, log = TRUE)
}

# If nu is supplied, it is held fixed and only (w, sigma2) are optimized.
joint_mode <- function(y, c0, C0, lambda, nu = NULL, tol = 1e-10,
                       maxit = 10000L) {
  fixed_nu <- !is.null(nu)
  if (!fixed_nu) nu <- 7
  sigma2 <- mean(y^2)
  lp_old <- -Inf
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    # Mode of w_i | y_i, sigma2, nu ~ Gamma((nu + 1) / 2, (nu + y_i^2 / sigma2) / 2)
    w <- (nu - 1) / (nu + y^2 / sigma2)
    # Mode of sigma2 | y, w
    sigma2 <- (C0 + sum(w * y^2) / 2) / (c0 + 1 + length(y) / 2)
    # Mode of nu | w (the objective is concave in nu)
    if (!fixed_nu) {
      nu <- exp(optimize(
        function(u) logpost_joint(y, sigma2, exp(u), w, c0, C0, lambda),
        log(c(1 + 1e-6, 1e6)), maximum = TRUE, tol = 1e-10)$maximum)
    }
    lp <- logpost_joint(y, sigma2, nu, w, c0, C0, lambda)
    if (lp - lp_old < tol * (1 + abs(lp))) break
    lp_old <- lp
  }
  list(sigma2 = sigma2, nu = nu, w = w, logpost = lp, iterations = it)
}

modes <- list(joint_mode(y, c0, C0, lambda, nu = 7),
              joint_mode(y, c0, C0, lambda))
knitr::kable(data.frame(model = c("t_7", "t_nu"),
                        sigma2 = sapply(modes, `[[`, "sigma2"),
                        nu = sapply(modes, `[[`, "nu"),
                        logpost = sapply(modes, `[[`, "logpost"),
                        iterations = sapply(modes, `[[`, "iterations")),
             digits = 3)

t_nu 0.527 10979.8 5608.022 7

Now we compute the conditional and the augmented DIC at the joint mode.

res <- array(NA_real_, c(2, 4, 10))
colnames(res) <- c("DIC_C", "pd_C", "DIC_A", "pd_A")
for (i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  d <- draws[[i + 1]]
  
  # Evaluate the log conditional likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogcondlik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logcondlik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Compute the average conditional deviance
  avgcondD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogcondlik)
  
  # Evaluate the log augmented likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogauglik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logauglik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  
  # Evaluate the deviances at the posterior mode (the same for all batches)
  sigma2_mode <- modes[[i]]$sigma2
  nu_mode <- modes[[i]]$nu
  w_mode <- modes[[i]]$w
  estcondD <- -2 * logcondlik(y, sigma2_mode, nu_mode, w_mode)
  
  # Compute conditional pd and conditional DIC
  res[i, "pd_C", ] <- avgcondD - estcondD
  res[i, "DIC_C", ] <- 2 * avgcondD - estcondD
  
  # Compute the average augmented deviance
  avgaugD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogauglik)
  
  # Evaluate the augmented deviance at the posterior mode
  estaugD <- -2 * logauglik(y, sigma2_mode, nu_mode, w_mode)
  
  # Compute augmented pd and augmented DIC
  res[i, "pd_A", ] <- avgaugD - estaugD
  res[i, "DIC_A", ] <- 2 * avgaugD - estaugD
}

mins <- apply(res, 1:2, min)
maxs <- apply(res, 1:2, max)
out <- matrix(paste0("[", roun(mins, 2), ", ", roun(maxs, 2), "]"),
              nrow = dim(res)[1])
colnames(out) <- colnames(res)
rownames(out) <- c("t_7", "t_nu")

The negative pDCp_D^C for the tνt_\nu model is a symptom of the degenerate joint mode: the exponential prior is the only thing that keeps ν\nu finite, so the mode sits at ν≈N/(2λ)≈11000\nu \approx N / (2\lambda) \approx 11000 with all wiw_i close to one, far away from the bulk of the posterior.

To compare the four plug-in points directly, we collect the conditional and the augmented DIC (and the corresponding pDp_D) in one table. The entries are the ranges over the ten batches.

dic_plugin <- function(i, nb = 10L) {
  d <- draws[[i + 1]]

  # Log conditional and augmented likelihood at all posterior draws
  alllogcondlik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logcondlik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  alllogauglik <- sapply(seq_along(d$sigma2s), function(j) {
    logauglik(y, d$sigma2s[j], d$nus[j], d$ws[j, ])
  })
  avgcondD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogcondlik)
  avgaugD <- -2 * batchMeans(alllogauglik)

  # Deviances at plug-in values (one value per batch)
  deviances <- function(sigma2, nu, w) {
    list(C = sapply(seq_len(nb), function(j)
           -2 * logcondlik(y, sigma2[j], nu[j], w[j, ])),
         A = sapply(seq_len(nb), function(j)
           -2 * logauglik(y, sigma2[j], nu[j], w[j, ])))
  }

  # Draw with highest joint posterior density within each batch
  alllogpost <- alllogauglik + dinvgamma(d$sigma2s, c0, C0, log = TRUE) +
    dexp(d$nus, lambda, log = TRUE)
  MAPind <- apply(batches(alllogpost), 2, which.max)
  idx <- MAPind + (seq_len(nb) - 1L) * (length(d$sigma2s) / nb)

  mode <- modes[[i]]
  plugins <- list(
    "MAP draw" = deviances(d$sigma2s[idx], d$nus[idx], d$ws[idx, , drop = FALSE]),
    "posterior mean" = deviances(batchMeans(d$sigma2s), batchMeans(d$nus),
                                 apply(d$ws, 2, batchMeans)),
    "posterior median" = deviances(batchMedians(d$sigma2s), batchMedians(d$nus),
                                   apply(d$ws, 2, batchMedians)),
    "joint mode" = deviances(rep(mode$sigma2, nb), rep(mode$nu, nb),
                             matrix(mode$w, nb, length(y), byrow = TRUE))
  )

  do.call(rbind, lapply(plugins, function(p) {
    vals <- cbind(DIC_C = 2 * avgcondD - p$C, pd_C = avgcondD - p$C,
                  DIC_A = 2 * avgaugD - p$A, pd_A = avgaugD - p$A)
    paste0("[", roun(apply(vals, 2, min)), ", ", roun(apply(vals, 2, max)), "]")
  }))
}

out <- rbind(dic_plugin(1), dic_plugin(2))
colnames(out) <- c("DIC_C", "pd_C", "DIC_A", "pd_A")
rownames(out) <- paste0(rep(c("t_7", "t_nu"), each = 4), ": ",
                        rep(c("MAP draw", "mean", "median", "joint mode"), 2))
knitr::kable(out)

Only the posterior mean and the posterior median give stable and plausible results for both models; the MAP draw is very noisy across batches with pDCp_D^C close to zero or negative, and the joint mode inflates pDp_D for t7t_7 and is degenerate for tνt_\nu.

Section 12.2.4: Widely applicable information criterion (WAIC)

Example 12.8: CHF exchange rate data: Testing normal vs. t using WAIC 

resWAIC <- array(NA_real_, c(3, 6, 10))
colnames(resWAIC) <-
  c("WAIC", "Dbiased", "phat", "WAIC_C", "Dbiased_C", "phat_C")
logpredlik <- Ehat <- Vhat <- logcondpredlik <- condEhat <- condVhat <-
  matrix(NA_real_, length(y), dim(resWAIC)[3])
for (i in 1:nrow(resWAIC)) {
  d <- draws[[i]]
  for (j in seq_along(y)) {
    logpredlikdraws <- dstudt(y[j], 0, sqrt(d$sigma2s), d$nus, log = TRUE)
    logpredlik[j, ] <- apply(batches(logpredlikdraws), 2, logmeanexp)
    Ehat[j, ] <- batchMeans(logpredlikdraws)
    Vhat[j, ] <- batchMeans(logpredlikdraws^2) - Ehat[j ,]^2
    if (i >= 2L) { # also evaluate the log conditional predictive likelihood
      logcondpredlikdraws <- dnorm(y[j], 0, sqrt(d$sigma2s / d$ws[, j]),
                                   log = TRUE)
      logcondpredlik[j, ] <- apply(batches(logcondpredlikdraws), 2, logmeanexp)
      condEhat[j, ] <- batchMeans(logcondpredlikdraws)
      condVhat[j, ] <- batchMeans(logcondpredlikdraws^2) - condEhat[j ,]^2
    }
  }
  resWAIC[i, "Dbiased", ] <- -2 * colSums(logpredlik)
  resWAIC[i, "phat", ] <- colSums(Vhat)
  resWAIC[i, "WAIC", ] <- resWAIC[i, "Dbiased", ] + 2 * resWAIC[i, "phat", ]
  if (i >= 2L) { # also evaluate the log conditional predictive likelihood
    resWAIC[i, "Dbiased_C", ] <- -2 * colSums(logcondpredlik)
    resWAIC[i, "phat_C", ] <- colSums(condVhat)
    resWAIC[i, "WAIC_C", ] <-
      resWAIC[i, "Dbiased_C", ] + 2 * resWAIC[i, "phat_C", ]
  }
}
mins <- apply(resWAIC, 1:2, min)
maxs <- apply(resWAIC, 1:2, max)
s <- c(1, 3:4, 6)
out <- matrix(paste0("[", roun(mins[, s], 2), ", ", roun(maxs[, s], 2), "]"),
              nrow = dim(resWAIC)[1])
out[out == "[NA, NA]"] <- ""
colnames(out) <- colnames(resWAIC)[s]
rownames(out) <- c("Gaussian", "t_7", "t_nu")
knitr::kable(out)

Section 12.3: Comparative model assessment through scoring rules

Section 12.3.1: Log predictive density scores

Example 12.?: CHF exchange rate data: Testing normal vs. t using LPDS

We first set the prior parameters as in Example 10.9.

nu <- 7
c10 <- c30 <- 3
C10 <- 3
C30 <- (nu - 2) / nu * C10

Next, we define our expanding estimation window.

trainends <- seq(2000, length(y) - 1)

Now we run the prediction on the expanding window and evaluate the one-step ahead predictive likelihood. For the normal model, this can be done analytically, for the Student t model, we need MCMC draws.

set.seed(seed)
M <- 100 / mcmcspeedup
burnin <- 100 / mcmcspeedup

LPDS <- matrix(NA_real_, 2, length(trainends))
for (i in seq_along(trainends)) {
  ytrain <- y[seq_len(trainends[i])]
  Ntrain <- length(ytrain)
  ytest <- y[trainends[i] + 1]
  
  # Normal model
  c1N <- c10 + 0.5 * Ntrain
  C1N <- C10 + 0.5 * sum(ytrain^2)
  LPDS[1, i] <- dstudt(ytest, 0, sqrt(C1N / c1N), 2 * c1N, log = TRUE)
  
  # Student t model
  draws <- sampler(ytrain, M, burnin, c30, C30, nu)
  logpreddraws <- dstudt(ytest, 0, sqrt(draws$sigma2s), draws$nus, log = TRUE)
  LPDS[2, i] <- logmeanexp(logpreddraws)
}

Now we compare and visualize.

logBF <- LPDS[2, ] - LPDS[1, ]
cumlogBF <- cumsum(logBF)
xs <- trainends + 1
plot(xs, y[xs], col = "darkgrey", xlab = "Time", ylab = "", yaxt = "n",
     type = "l")
axis(4)
mtext("CHF-USD daily percentage log returns", side = 4, line = 1.5)
abline(h = 0, lty = 3, col = "darkgray", lwd = 1.5)
par(new = TRUE)
plot(xs, cumlogBF, col = rgb(logBF < 0, 0, logBF > 0, .5), type = "b",
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", pch = 16, lwd = 2)
axis(2)
mtext("Cumulative log BF", side = 2, line = 1.5)
legend("topleft", c(paste0("Log BF > 0 (", round(100 * mean(logBF > 0)), "%)"),
                    paste0("Log BF < 0 (", round(100 * mean(logBF < 0)), "%)")),
       col = rgb(c(0, 1), 0, c(1, 0), .5), pch = 16, lty = 1, lwd = 2)
